nodes.label: Cartoon Vector Mascot Style
nodes.rationale: Bold black outlines, cel-shaded flats, simplified anatomy, sticker-like isolation on white with an oval ground shadow. Fintech-mascot illustration, not photorealism or a UI screenshot.

nodes.label: F Bank
nodes.rationale: Named brand on the hoodie chest lockup. The mascot exists to personify this bank as friendly, youthful, and trustworthy.

nodes.label: Banking Shield Metaphor
nodes.rationale: A shield for a head encodes protection and trust — the visual language of banking security — while the smile and hoodie keep the same idea from feeling institutional or severe.

nodes.label: F Bank Mascot Character
nodes.rationale: Full-body anthropomorphic brand mascot for F Bank: a smiling shield-headed figure in matching green streetwear, isolated on white with a soft drop shadow. Delivered as a GIF89a (~357x358) web asset so the character can sit in product UI as an animated, approachable face of the bank rather than a static logo.

nodes.label: Green Streetwear Uniform
nodes.rationale: Dark green pullover hoodie with white drawstrings and white-gloved hands; matching joggers with a white side stripe; white sneakers with green heel/toe caps and a lime F on each tongue. Casual athletic kit, not a suit or bank-teller costume.

nodes.label: Two-Tone Shield Head
nodes.rationale: The head is a heraldic shield split vertically: mint/light green on the left, forest green on the right, with large cartoon eyes, simple black brows, and a small smile. No hair, ears, or nose. The shield-as-face is the character's defining silhouette.

nodes.label: Shield-as-Face Security Metaphor
nodes.rationale: The character's entire head is a heraldic shield, encoding protection and trust as the face of the brand.

nodes.label: F BANK Mascot (Look Aside)
nodes.rationale: Anthropomorphic streetwear character makes a bank brand feel friendly and youth-oriented while the shield head still signals protection.

nodes.label: Approachable Bank Branding
nodes.rationale: Cartoon eyes, a small smile, hoodie-and-sweats, and white sneakers soften a financial brand into a casual, kid-friendly mascot.

nodes.label: API_ALLOWED_PREFIXES
nodes.rationale: Default allow-list: /api/v1/health and /api/v1/cqa/. Paths outside return 404 without reaching FastAPI, so Data Studio uploads and training are not public.

nodes.label: Web Server /api Proxy
nodes.rationale: Forwards allowed /api paths to API_UPSTREAM. Strips hop-by-hop headers, adds X-Forwarded-*, keeps Host unchanged so API host and origin guards still work. Rejects %2f/%5c/\ /.. path tricks with 400 bad_path.

nodes.label: OriginGuard
nodes.rationale: Refuses POST/PUT/PATCH/DELETE whose Origin is neither an allowed web origin nor the API itself. Requests without Origin (curl, tests) are allowed. Complements CORS, which cannot stop form POSTs.

nodes.label: Request Middleware Stack
nodes.rationale: Middleware runs in reverse add order: TrustedHost → CORS → OriginGuard → GZip (>2 KB) → thin Pydantic route → service. Routes stay thin so logic can be tested without HTTP via create_app(Settings(data_dir=<temp>)).

nodes.label: No Login Authentication
nodes.rationale: Deliberate non-goal for a localhost tool. Exposure is controlled only by the web server allow-list and API_READ_ONLY. Defends against a malicious page in the same browser, not remote identity.

nodes.label: DEGRADED single-context banner
nodes.rationale: A silent degraded critique is a failed critique. The report's first line MUST be a banner when degraded.

nodes.label: Dual-agent critique
nodes.rationale: Assessment A and B MUST run as two isolated sub-agents whenever a sub-agent tool is exposed. Inline is a degraded run.

nodes.label: Impeccable hooks
nodes.rationale: Manages the design detector hook that auto-runs after UI file edits and surfaces findings.

nodes.label: Branded Green Hoodie Outfit
nodes.rationale: Casual hoodie, matching joggers, and sneakers keep the bank mascot streetwear-friendly rather than corporate or armored.

nodes.label: F Bank Mascot
nodes.rationale: Default web-app mascot GIF: an anthropomorphic green shield character in casual streetwear, designed to make a bank brand feel protective and approachable at once.

nodes.label: Default Idle Pose
nodes.rationale: Front-facing stand with hands in the hoodie pocket and a smile is the default/idle state encoded by mascot-default.gif.

nodes.label: Two-Tone Shield Head
nodes.rationale: The head is a heraldic shield split on a jagged diagonal into lime and forest green, with large cartoon eyes, a wide toothy smile, and small side nubs — a security/protection metaphor rendered as a friendly face.

nodes.label: Appeals and Reviewer Overrides
nodes.rationale: Override is always a new answer, never a typed-in score; engine recomputes final_score. Original vs final score both kept. Worked example: fx-ru-001 solution none→full moved 66.3 to 96.3.

nodes.label: Versioned Checklist
nodes.rationale: Sections and up to 60 criteria with weight, answer type (binary/scale/options), N/A and severe-error rules. Criteria/sections/scoring changes save a new immutable version; evaluations store a full copy. Optimistic concurrency via base_version (409 stale_checklist).

nodes.label: Development Sample Checklist
nodes.rationale: Unofficial placeholder created by POST /cqa/checklists/dev-sample. Must be replaced by the official checklist. Scores from it are not real quality results.

nodes.label: CQA Scoring Engine
nodes.rationale: compute_score is a pure function using Fraction so the same answers always give the same score. Only place a score is computed. N/A weight redistributed; severe_error_policy flag_only or zero_total; rounding once at the end.

nodes.rationale: audio_url is an organizer player page, not a file. GET /cqa/conversations/{id}/audio extracts signed MP3 from <source>/<audio> only from ATLAS_CQA_AUDIO_HOSTS. Failures return player_only.

nodes.label: Conversation Quality Analytics (CQA)
nodes.rationale: The deployed product area. Imports call-centre conversations in Russian, Kazakh and English, evaluates them against a versioned checklist through a pluggable evaluator, scores with a deterministic engine, and handles appeals with an audit trail.

nodes.label: CQA HTTP Endpoints /api/v1/cqa
nodes.rationale: 29 endpoints under /api/v1/cqa. Default public allow-list exposes all of them through the web server, including imports, evaluations, checklist edits and appeal decisions.

nodes.label: CQA Evaluation Pipeline
nodes.rationale: Separates three jobs often mixed: evaluator only answers; contract checks answers strictly; scoring engine turns answers into points. Appeals change the final score only through new answers, never by editing numbers.

nodes.label: Evaluation State Machine
nodes.rationale: pending → running → completed|failed. After restart, pending is re-queued and running is failed as interrupted. Queue snapshots checklist version and transcript hash.

nodes.label: CQA Conversation Ingestion
nodes.rationale: POST /cqa/imports fetches a group server-side so the browser never sees the signed URL. source_url_for replaces only group_id. Per-record parse; nothing invented. Transcript SHA-256 detects create/unchanged/updated/source_conflict.

nodes.label: Hook Ignore Actions
nodes.rationale: Prefer the narrowest exception. Self-serve stops at ignore-value; ignore-file and ignore-rule require asking the user first.

nodes.label: Two-Tier Detector
nodes.rationale: Per-edit hook surfaces only mechanical immediate-tier problems; Stop hook runs the full rule set over session UI files. Cursor has no Stop deep pass; Copilot keeps full detector per edit.

nodes.label: Design Detector Hook
nodes.rationale: Runs the impeccable design detector on design-relevant file edits. Toggled per project via .impeccable/config.json; never edit that file by hand from this command.

nodes.label: Optimize Command
nodes.rationale: Performance is a feature. Identify the actual bottleneck for THIS interface, fix it, then measure. Don't optimize what isn't slow.

nodes.label: Thinking Pose
nodes.rationale: Hand on chin and upward glance humanize a wait or consider state in the web UI.

nodes.label: ATLAS Backend
nodes.rationale: One Python process (FastAPI, Pydantic v2, pandas, scikit-learn) that stores everything as files on local disk with no database. Serves CQA and Data Studio on a shared foundation.

nodes.label: Node Web Server apps/web-server
nodes.rationale: Dependency-free Node server that serves apps/web and forwards /api/* to FastAPI so the browser talks to one origin. Public boundary behind Cloudflare: decides which API paths the internet can reach.

nodes.label: ATLAS Backend Report
nodes.rationale: Explains the ATLAS backend from commit 3c6abb7 on deploy/cicd: FastAPI in apps/api (~9400 lines, 74 HTTP endpoints) and the Node proxy in apps/web-server, covering CQA and Data Studio with live API examples generated 7 November 2026.

nodes.label: File-Based Storage No Database
nodes.rationale: Everything is files on local disk; CQA keeps conversations, evaluations and appeals in memory. Fine for hackathon volumes, not millions.

nodes.label: compose.prod.yml Deployment
nodes.rationale: api not published to host (expose 8000); web on 127.0.0.1:3000 with Cloudflare Tunnel. host.docker.internal lets a host model service count as local for the http adapter.

nodes.label: ExperimentManager
nodes.rationale: 2-thread pool that trains models in the background. Interrupted trainings are marked failed on restart.

nodes.label: Custom control gesture verification
nodes.rationale: Screenshots and resized viewports verify layout, never a gesture. Name what stayed untested; unreachable hardware is a reported gap, not a blocker.

nodes.label: Plate
nodes.rationale: A plate is the region regenerated at asset resolution from the comp crop: UI text and page chrome removed. Crops are references, never shipping pixels.

nodes.label: Do not redesign (asset production)
nodes.rationale: Preserve the reference's visual role, silhouette, palette, lighting, material, texture, camera angle, and composition unless the parent explicitly asks for a change. Production cleanup, not new art direction.

nodes.label: Doctor Finding Severities
nodes.rationale: Severity says what should happen: auto runs --fix without asking; mention states each finding; route names a command and runs only if the user asks.

nodes.label: Schema Drift
nodes.rationale: Artifact written by an older Impeccable: unread fields, newly expected fields, retired locations. Mechanical; doctor repairs most of it.

nodes.label: Tool Version Drift
nodes.rationale: Installed skill older than published; impeccable context reports UPDATE_AVAILABLE and npx impeccable update fixes it. Not doctor's job.

nodes.label: Truth Drift
nodes.rationale: Code moved on and the document no longer describes it. Doctor hands a specific gap to document (DESIGN.md) or init (PRODUCT.md) rather than a vague suspicion.

nodes.label: Impeccable Doctor Command
nodes.rationale: Maintenance, not design: report and repair drift between Impeccable artifacts and what the installed version reads, without redesigning or opening files outside the report.

nodes.label: F Bank Mascot
nodes.rationale: Anthropomorphized two-tone green bank shield in a casual hoodie and sneakers, waving to greet users as a friendly, non-corporate coach rather than a stiff institutional mark.

nodes.label: Material Design 3
nodes.rationale: Material Design 3 governs structure, navigation, and interaction in every visitor mode; brand expresses through Material's theming.

nodes.label: Android slop test
nodes.rationale: Would a fluent Android user trust this app, or trip on off-spec components? The most common tell is an iOS app wearing Android's skin.

nodes.label: Web to native reconform
nodes.rationale: Reconform, don't reflow. Replace web navigation with the platform's model; the slop test is the acceptance bar.

nodes.label: ATLAS Submits Nothing
nodes.rationale: No connection to the competition platform; a team member uploads deliverables by hand after review.

nodes.label: Every Number Carries Provenance
nodes.rationale: ATLAS never manufactures conclusions; automated text is limited to verifiable descriptive statistics.

nodes.label: Carbonize Cleanup
nodes.rationale: Accepted variant is stitched with helper markers; rewrite into permanent form before the next poll or dead @scope rules accumulate. live-complete refuses while leftovers remain.

nodes.label: Live Config Drift
nodes.rationale: Orphan HTML files under common page roots not covered by files. Never auto-update; the user decides.

nodes.label: Live CSP Detection
nodes.rationale: First-time only. Allow http://localhost:8400 on script-src and connect-src, development-only. Consent required before auto-patch.

nodes.label: Generate Command
nodes.rationale: Fast lane into live mode: name an element, direction, and count; boot helper, splice variants, wait for accept. Web only; native projects decline and offer bolder or quieter.

nodes.label: Live Variant Mode
nodes.rationale: Select elements in the browser, pick a design action, get HTML+CSS variants hot-swapped via HMR. Requires local checkout; production injection unsupported. _instructions wins over recollection.

nodes.label: .impeccable/live/config.json
nodes.rationale: One-time live-mode setup. files are HTML the browser actually loads. Hard-excluded: node_modules and .git.

nodes.label: Overdrive Command
nodes.rationale: Push an interface past conventional limits using the full power of the browser. Context decides what extraordinary means. Enhances how an interface feels, not what a product does.

nodes.label: Identity Lock
nodes.rationale: Live varies expression within identity, not between identities. Absence of DESIGN.md is never an excuse; extract from CSS, computed styles, and siblings. Departure requires explicit redesign intent.

nodes.label: Propose Before Building
nodes.rationale: Highest potential to misfire. Think through 2-3 directions, get the user's pick before writing any code. Live mode skips this because it is non-interactive.

nodes.label: Operate Four World Contributions
nodes.rationale: World lends only type, palette, density, and one signature move. Never supplies layout, navigation model, or controls.

nodes.label: World as Page Carrier
nodes.rationale: A facade, shutter, or book can be what the page is built on; a viewport painted whole as a poster with no working parts is a picture of the world, not its website.

nodes.label: Read Frame and Column
nodes.rationale: World owns the frame (masthead, rail, ground, openers); the reading column stays calm at about 60-75 characters. World never supplies reading order.

nodes.label: Code-Led Build Path
nodes.rationale: No page comp. Ambition lives in FIRST VIEWPORT and named signature interaction; finish reviewer audits those promises in behavior.

nodes.label: impeccable concept-seed
nodes.rationale: On a new or replacement world, writing artifact code before this script has run is a contract violation. The roll keeps every run from converging on the category default.

nodes.label: Standing Exit Canon
nodes.rationale: Every direction round offers the category standard as the user's door, never recommended, never weighed against the roll.

nodes.label: Operate Mode Depth
nodes.rationale: Extended depth for app UIs, dashboards, tools. Read surfaces take this file's typography and consistency rules plus SKILL.md Read mode.

nodes.label: iOS Slop Test
nodes.rationale: Would a fluent iPhone user trust this app, or pause at off-spec controls? The tell is ported from a website.

nodes.label: Operate Mode Rules
nodes.rationale: Visitor came to get a job done. The page is first a working product of its category; the world serves it.

nodes.label: Persuade and Experience Mode Rules
nodes.rationale: On these surfaces the design is what the visitor judges, so the world may own and structure the page.

nodes.label: Read Mode Rules
nodes.rationale: Visitor came to understand something. The page is first a document of its kind, framed by the world.

nodes.label: Product Slop Test
nodes.rationale: Whether a category-fluent user can trust the interface immediately. Failure mode is strangeness without purpose. The bar is earned familiarity.

nodes.label: Two Local Processes
nodes.rationale: Next.js web app and FastAPI service both bind to 127.0.0.1; the browser talks to the API directly with no Next.js proxy.

nodes.label: Hybrid Evaluation Mode
nodes.rationale: Gemma answers official criteria matching the template; GPT answers custom or changed official criteria. Weight and section changes do not count as changed.

nodes.label: Model Never Produces the Score
nodes.rationale: raw_score is recorded for comparison but never used; points, weights, N/A redistribution and rounding happen in the engine so replacing the model changes answers, not arithmetic.

nodes.label: Local-First Workbench
nodes.rationale: Next.js plus FastAPI on the machine; data stays local; no external AI calls, analytics SDKs, or third-party uploads.

nodes.label: Motion thesis
nodes.rationale: A generic fade-and-rise, hover lift, parallax layer, or scroll reveal is not a thesis. The focal moment must come from this product and surface concept.

nodes.label: Experience mode
nodes.rationale: The visitor is inside the work itself. Let the artifact lead from the first viewport; the interface recedes.

nodes.label: Operate mode
nodes.rationale: The visitor completes a task. Scanability, consistency, native expectations, and the real usage scene outrank expression.

nodes.label: Persuade mode
nodes.rationale: The visitor decides and acts; design is the product. Landing pages, marketing, campaigns, pricing.

nodes.label: Read mode
nodes.rationale: The visitor understands something. Structure for comprehension, then make the reading experience worth staying in.

nodes.label: Visitor mode
nodes.rationale: The mode names what the visitor's success looks like on this surface, chosen from the requested surface not the product, and persisted only in that surface brief.

nodes.label: Decoration without purpose is animation debt
nodes.norm_label: decoration without purpose is animation debt
nodes.rationale: Use motion to explain state, relationship, and hierarchy, or to create one authored moment the surface has earned.

nodes.label: Delight is product character, not generic whimsy
nodes.norm_label: delight is product character, not generic whimsy
nodes.rationale: Delight is product character revealed through a useful interaction, a humane response, or an unexpectedly considered detail. Do not manufacture a celebration for an ordinary click.

nodes.label: Scale ambition to surface mode
nodes.rationale: Persuade and Experience get full commitment: bold, distinct work with a point of view. On Operate and Read, ambition shows as precision and restraint, and familiar patterns earn their place.

nodes.label: Analysis Plug-in Registry
nodes.rationale: @register_analysis with column_param kinds means a new analysis needs no frontend change. GET /analyses lists parameter JSON schemas.

nodes.label: CqaStore
nodes.rationale: JSON persistence under cqa/. Loads all JSON into memory at start-up and write-through on change. Corrupt files are skipped, never silently rewritten. Conversation files use an 8-character hash suffix to avoid case-insensitive collisions.

nodes.label: create_app Factory and Lifespan
nodes.rationale: app/main.py builds FastAPI, registers middleware/error handlers/routers, and in lifespan creates Workspace, DatasetService, ExperimentManager, ReportStore and CqaService on app.state. Shutdown stops both thread pools and cancels queued work.

nodes.label: Data Studio
nodes.rationale: Local-first analysis workbench (datasets, profiling, charts, recipes, models, findings). By default the public web server does not forward these endpoints.

nodes.label: Workspace File Storage
nodes.rationale: Owns every Data Studio path under ATLAS_DATA_DIR. Writes are atomic (temp file then os.replace). LRU cache of up to 4 loaded tables keyed by dataset id and mtime.

nodes.label: Single Uvicorn Worker
nodes.rationale: One worker is required: the CQA store and both thread pools live in process memory, so several processes would each hold their own diverging copy.

nodes.label: Entry Atomicity
nodes.rationale: Mark an entry applied only when every op in that entry is applied. If one op fails, undo any source edits already made for that same entry.

nodes.label: impeccable context launcher
nodes.rationale: Run once per session from the skill folder; loads PRODUCT.md, DESIGN.md, the matching surface brief, and native-platform guidance. Launcher failure does not block planning or editing.

nodes.label: Ground truth is the shipped artifact
nodes.norm_label: ground truth is the shipped artifact
nodes.rationale: Every token and rule must be evidenced by the built code, never by what was planned. A rulebook written before the build gets defended against reality instead of describing it.

nodes.label: Visual authority is evidence, not a filename
nodes.norm_label: visual authority is evidence, not a filename
nodes.rationale: Missing DESIGN.md alone does not make a project greenfield; new-work decides whether to preserve, expand, or replace the incumbent world.

nodes.label: design-md-drift Finding
nodes.rationale: Counts commits to visual source directories since DESIGN.md was last edited; a commit count is not a contradiction and must not be asserted as staleness.

nodes.label: DESIGN.md Frontmatter Token Schema
nodes.rationale: Stitch Zod schema accepts only colors, typography, rounded, spacing, components. Token refs use {path.to.token}. Component sub-tokens limited to 8 props.

nodes.label: Document Scan Mode
nodes.rationale: Default path: extract tokens from code then confirm descriptive language. Use when there is code to analyze.

nodes.label: .impeccable/design.json Sidecar
nodes.rationale: schemaVersion 2 carries what Stitch cannot hold: tonal ramps, shadows, motion, breakpoints, HTML/CSS snippets, narrative. Extends frontmatter; does not duplicate primitives.

nodes.label: DESIGN.md
nodes.rationale: Captures the current visual design system so AI agents stay on-brand. Tokens are normative; prose provides application context. Never silently overwrite an existing file.

nodes.label: Extract Flow
nodes.rationale: Identify reusable patterns, components, and tokens then consolidate into the design system. Extract only things used 3+ times with the same intent.

nodes.label: Polish Command
nodes.rationale: Refinement, never concealed redesign. Preserve the incumbent visual world. If the concept is wrong, recommend redesign or bolder instead of smuggling a replacement.

nodes.label: Named Rules
nodes.rationale: Memorable citable doctrines of the form The [Name] Rule. Aim for 1-3 per section; stickier for AI consumers than bullet lists.

nodes.label: Three-Plus Reuse Rule
nodes.rationale: Premature abstraction is worse than duplication; only extract patterns used 3+ times with the same intent.

nodes.label: Working Memory Rule
nodes.rationale: Humans can hold ≤4 items in working memory at once (Miller's Law revised by Cowan, 2001).

nodes.label: Amplify what the system already owns
nodes.norm_label: amplify what the system already owns
nodes.rationale: The reflex of reaching for more effects is the opposite of bold. The bolder version should look more like the same brand, not less.

nodes.label: Scope is sovereign
nodes.rationale: Touch only the named target. Do not restyle neighbors or add colors, fonts, radii, shadows, or system primitives the surface does not already own.

nodes.label: Kicker / eyebrow ban
nodes.rationale: A kicker or eyebrow above a heading is a ban, not a default: no brief earns it back. The heading carries its own weight.

nodes.label: Never canonize a craft-floor refusal
nodes.rationale: An element the floor bans is recorded as a defect the build carries, never as a design-system rule for future surfaces to inherit.

nodes.label: Simplicity removes obstacles, not features
nodes.rationale: Simplicity is not about removing features. It's about removing obstacles between users and their goals. Every element should justify its existence.

nodes.label: Harden Command
nodes.rationale: Designs that only work with perfect data are not production-ready. Harden against extreme inputs, errors, languages, and network conditions.

nodes.label: Layout Command
nodes.rationale: Turns product priority into reading order, grouping, rhythm, and usable space. Diagnose the structural problem before moving boxes. Identity replacement belongs to new-work.

nodes.label: Onboard Command
nodes.rationale: Onboarding's job is not to teach the product. Its job is to get people to the moment that proves the product is worth their time.

nodes.label: Color Refinement
nodes.rationale: Desaturate to 70-85%, neutrals do the work, color as 10% accent, tinted grays instead of pure gray.

nodes.label: Quiet Design
nodes.rationale: Reduce visual intensity without losing personality; quiet without intent collapses to generic gray-on-white.
nodes.source_location: Quiet design is harder than bold design

nodes.label: The Darkroom
nodes.rationale: Near-black charcoal surfaces so the brightest things on screen are the data: chart marks, table values, metric deltas.

nodes.label: Scenario C Regression
nodes.source_location: Scenario C: regression, or a forecast-like target

nodes.label: Welcoming Brand Persona
nodes.rationale: Smile, slow wave, hand on hip, and casual clothes present the bank as friendly and low-pressure rather than formal or institutional.

nodes.label: F Bank Mascot
nodes.rationale: Anthropomorphic brand character: a two-tone green shield for a head, cartoon eyes and a wide smile, white gloves, and casual streetwear. Posed waving with the other hand on the hip so the bank feels friendly and approachable.

nodes.label: Shield Head
nodes.rationale: The character's head is the bank shield logo turned into a face: darker green on the left, brighter green on the right, split by a lightning-bolt F mark, with large eyes and a grin.

nodes.label: Slow Wave Loop
nodes.rationale: The GIF is a slow repeating wave, not a fast attention grab. A calmer loop suits a persistent home-page mascot.

nodes.label: Streetwear Costume
nodes.rationale: Dark green hoodie, matching joggers with a small F on the thigh, and chunky white-green sneakers dress a bank mascot like a casual youth character instead of a suit.

nodes.label: Wave Greeting
nodes.rationale: Primary action of the asset: right arm raised, white-gloved palm facing the viewer, used as a hello on the home screen.

nodes.label: craft command
nodes.rationale: Deprecated alias for an ordinary new-work request; adds nothing.

nodes.label: Impeccable
nodes.rationale: Gives tools and permission to make out-of-distribution craft: production-grade code, a clear POV, grasp of client and user need, and exceptional craft. Not for backend-only or non-UI tasks.

nodes.label: craft adds no setup or quality behavior
nodes.norm_label: craft adds no setup or quality behavior
nodes.rationale: craft is a deprecated alias for ordinary new visual work. It adds no setup, interview, checkpoint, tool, or quality behavior. Do not tell users they need to invoke craft.

nodes.label: Finish the job
nodes.rationale: No hedging, no shortcuts: the deliverable is complete, except assets the user must provide.

nodes.label: Loaded symbols stay out of the decoration
nodes.norm_label: loaded symbols stay out of the decoration
nodes.rationale: A subject's world does not license emblems tied to militarism, supremacy, or hate movements as motifs; reach for that world's neutral forms instead. Content that documents such a symbol as fact stays as it is.

nodes.label: Refinement preserves; redesign replaces
nodes.rationale: Refinement keeps incumbent identity, behavior, copy, and everything outside scope. Redesign keeps product truth and constraints but treats the old look as anti-reference; never split the difference into polish on the discarded look.

nodes.label: The brief wins
nodes.rationale: Honor pinned aesthetics, eras, materials, fonts, and palettes even when they conflict with a saturated-pattern warning. Redirecting a clear brief toward the agent's taste is failure.

nodes.label: Verify by looking at the rendered result
nodes.norm_label: verify by looking at the rendered result
nodes.rationale: Verify at the sizes it ships at, and batch the checks: fix what one look shows before looking again, rather than screenshotting after every tweak.

nodes.label: buildPath Config Key
nodes.rationale: comp or code in .impeccable/config.json; Operate and Read surfaces are code-led whatever it holds. An unread value does not fall back.

nodes.label: Document Seed Mode
nodes.rationale: Pre-implementation: PRODUCT.md required, then new-work visual-world workshop. Writes directional seed without token scales or design.json sidecar.

nodes.label: Init buildPath Question
nodes.rationale: Asked once when image generation exists and no buildPath is recorded. Comp-first vs code-first. Workflow setting, never PRODUCT.md. Unset is a working state.

nodes.label: Comp-Led Build Path
nodes.rationale: Chosen card's comp is law. Build runs as a measured state machine: comps, spec, plates, hero, sections, motion, responsive. Operate and Read surfaces are code-led whatever the project records.

nodes.label: Init Flow
nodes.rationale: Captures durable product truth in PRODUCT.md. Does not invent a visual world or write DESIGN.md.

nodes.label: Direction Contract
nodes.rationale: Six blocks in the surface brief: THESIS, OWN-WORLD, STORY, FIRST VIEWPORT, FORM, FINISH. Never copy into implementation source or browser-delivered artifacts.

nodes.label: New Visual Work
nodes.rationale: Flow for a new surface or replacement visual identity. PRODUCT.md owns product truth; DESIGN.md owns durable visual decisions; a surface brief keeps per-route strategy.

nodes.label: workspace-platform-native-evidence
nodes.rationale: Workspace with native build files inheriting a web root record never loads ios.md or android.md; repair is a child PRODUCT.md.

nodes.label: Product Platform
nodes.rationale: Bare value web, ios, android, or adaptive. Mobile web remains web; a native wrapper around a website does not make its design language native.

nodes.label: iOS Simulator Verification
nodes.rationale: Screenshots come from the Simulator via xcrun simctl, never a browser. Dark Mode and Dynamic Type belong in the pass.

nodes.label: PRODUCT.md
nodes.rationale: Confirmed facts only. Visual worlds, palettes, and surface strategy do not belong here.

nodes.label: HIG Conformance
nodes.rationale: Governs structure, navigation, and interaction in every visitor mode; brand expresses through tint, type, motion, and content.

nodes.label: Evaluator Contract cqa-eval/1
nodes.rationale: Single seam between the backend and any AI model. Model receives EvaluationRequest and must return ModelOutput. Strict validation lists every problem; claimed raw_score is stored for comparison but never used.

nodes.label: EvaluatorAdapter
nodes.rationale: Turns EvaluationRequest into ModelOutput and never scores. Every module in app/cqa/adapters/ is imported at start-up; a broken adapter is logged and skipped. Team models subclass EvaluatorAdapter and register_adapter.

nodes.label: HTTP Evaluator Adapter
nodes.rationale: POSTs EvaluationRequest JSON to ATLAS_CQA_EVALUATOR_URL (8 MB, 180 s). Only loopback hosts (localhost, 127.0.0.1, ::1, host.docker.internal) unless ATLAS_CQA_EVALUATOR_ALLOW_REMOTE=true, so transcripts never leave the machine by accident.

nodes.label: Mock Evaluator Adapter
nodes.rationale: Development only, not AI. Answers from SHA-256 of (conversation, criterion, definition); evidence is a real transcript line. Explanations start with [DEV MOCK]; overview counts mock_results. Default ATLAS_CQA_EVALUATOR=mock.

nodes.label: Model Service POST cqa-eval/1
nodes.rationale: Outbound CQA call: POST the contract request to a local model service (example ATLAS_CQA_EVALUATOR_URL=http://127.0.0.1:9000/evaluate). One of only three outbound network calls the backend makes.

nodes.label: Team Model In-Process Adapter
nodes.rationale: Documented pattern: apps/api/app/cqa/adapters/team_model.py with @register_adapter("team-model"). Selected via ATLAS_CQA_EVALUATOR=team-model or per-request adapter field.

nodes.label: Contract Evidence Validation
nodes.rationale: Every non-N/A answer needs evidence or an inspected span. Quotes must occur in the cited message (case/space/quote/ellipsis insensitive); matched character range is stored for UI highlighting.

nodes.label: Content-driven breakpoints
nodes.rationale: Don't chase device sizes; let content tell you where to break. Three breakpoints usually suffice (640, 768, 1024px).

nodes.label: Mobile-first responsive design
nodes.rationale: Start with base styles for mobile, use min-width queries to layer complexity. Desktop-first means mobile loads unnecessary styles first.

nodes.label: Translate idioms; never transplant them
nodes.rationale: Rebuild navigation and controls in the target's vocabulary; carry over the brand's expressive layer through the target's theming system.

nodes.label: Restructure, don't stretch
nodes.rationale: A scaled-up phone UI on a tablet is the failure mode. Use size classes (iOS) / window size classes (Android) to switch structure.

nodes.label: Detect input method, not just screen size
nodes.norm_label: detect input method, not just screen size
nodes.rationale: Screen size does not tell you input method. Use pointer and hover media queries. Don't rely on hover for functionality.

nodes.label: Adaptation is rethinking, not scaling
nodes.rationale: The trap is treating adaptation as scaling. The job is rethinking the experience for the new context.

nodes.label: System Back always works
nodes.rationale: Honor the predictive Back gesture and Back button; never trap the user or hijack the gesture.

nodes.label: Audit documents, does not fix
nodes.rationale: Don't fix issues; document them for other commands to address. This is a code-level audit, not a design critique.

nodes.label: Color roles
nodes.rationale: Build roles, not a bag of swatches. Decoration without a relationship to hierarchy, state, content, or the visual world is not a color strategy.

nodes.label: Native audit report skeleton mirrors web audit
nodes.norm_label: native audit report skeleton mirrors web audit
nodes.rationale: The report skeleton mirrors audit.md; keep the two in sync when changing it. No browser tooling or impeccable detect applies on native.

nodes.label: Floor holds mechanics, never picks direction
nodes.norm_label: floor holds mechanics, never picks direction
nodes.rationale: A pinned brief or the committed visual world overrides anything here. With every check green, spend the page on the committed world, and when torn between refined and committed, commit.

nodes.label: Region Map
nodes.rationale: Names what is visible in the approved comp before asset production; not a page build or asset approval.

nodes.label: Comp Approval Point
nodes.rationale: No substitute and no skip: code does not begin until the user approves a direction or delegates.
